FCCANALYSIS-RUN(1) fccanalysis-run man page FCCANALYSIS-RUN(1)

NAME

fccanalysis-run - run FCC analysis

SYNOPSIS

fccanalysis run analysis-script [-h | --help] [-i INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...] | --input INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...] | --input-file-list LIST_FILE] [--output OUTPUT] [--n-events NEVENTS] [--test] [--bench] [-j NCPUS | --ncpus NCPUS | --n-threads NTHREADS] [-g] [--graph-path GRAPH_PATH] [--use-data-source] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--output-format {ttree,rntuple}] [-a ANALYSIS_NAME | --analysis-name ANALYSIS_NAME] [--use-eos-mount] [-s SAMPLE_NAME | --sample-name SAMPLE_NAME] [--n-chunks N_CHUNKS] [--stride STRIDE] [--test-file TEST_FILE] [-- ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS]

DESCRIPTION

fccanalysis-run will run analysis provided in the analysis script on the current machine, i.e. locally. The analysis itself can be divided into several stages, if desired. For all those stages fccanalysis-run is used.

When using fccanalysis-run the analysis is running in the managed mode, where the RDataFrame is steered by the framework and users can control only some aspects of the running with additional global attributes, see fccanalysis-script(7).

INPUT PATHS

An input path may name a local ROOT file, a local directory, a mounted /eos/... path, an XRootD URL, or an HTTP(S) file URL. Directory discovery keeps immediate .root files only; it does not recurse into subdirectories.

HTTP(S) URLs name individual files; HTTP directory discovery is not supported. Other paths ending in .root name one file; remaining paths are treated as directories. XRootD directories are listed through xrdfs. For XRootD URLs, the .root suffix is checked before the query string. File queries are preserved. Directory discovery requires URLs without queries. Duplicate input paths within one sample are rejected after path normalization. Explicit paths and input-list entries retain their supplied order; files discovered within each directory are sorted by path.

CERN /eos/experiment/..., /eos/user/..., /eos/home-<initial>/..., and /eos/project/... paths are translated to XRootD URLs before discovery, even when mounted locally. Use an explicit root:// URL for other EOS namespaces or for storage outside CERN.

For modern Analysis scripts, --use-eos-mount keeps EOS paths on the local FUSE mount for discovery and reading; there is no automatic fallback to XRootD. Explicit root:// URLs remain remote. Legacy RDFanalysis scripts always rewrite supported EOS paths. The old --no-filepath-rewrites option remains available as a deprecated alias for --use-eos-mount. The --apply-filepath-rewrites option remains accepted with a deprecation warning.

OPTIONS

analysis-script
Path to analysis script.
-h, --help
Prints short help message and exits.
-i INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...], --input INPUT_PATH [INPUT_PATH ...]
Directly specify one or more input paths. See INPUT PATHS for supported files and directories. This option cannot be combined with --input-file-list. It takes precedence over the files determined from the samples attribute (or its deprecated process_list alias) of the analysis.
--input-file-list LIST_FILE
Specify file containing list of input ROOT files. This option cannot be combined with --input. It takes precedence over the files determined from the samples attribute (or its deprecated process_list alias) of the analysis. Each input ROOT file needs to be on a separate line. Directory entries are not expanded. Blank lines and lines beginning with "#" are ignored.
--output OUTPUT
Specify an output file for test mode or an independent sample with one chunk. Script-defined samples use their output stems and output directory instead.
--n-events NEVENTS, --nevents NEVENTS
Specify the maximum number of events per sample, overriding script settings. Limits are ignored with a warning when a sample has multiple chunks.
--test
Run over the test file in a single job. If --input or --input-file-list is supplied, it is ignored with a warning.
--use-data-source
Load events through podio::DataSource.
--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
Set global output directory for the analysis.
--output-format {ttree, rntuple}
Specify the output ROOT file format. This option overrides the analysis script's output_format setting.
Default: follow the format of the events TTree or RNTuple in the first input file.
-a ANALYSIS_NAME, --analysis-name ANALYSIS_NAME
Set analysis name, mostly used for the output path.
--use-eos-mount
Use mounted EOS paths for discovery and reading in modern Analysis scripts. The deprecated --no-filepath-rewrites option remains as an alias.
-s SAMPLE_NAME, --sample-name SAMPLE_NAME
Set sample name, mostly used for the output path. Used when running over an independent sample (i.e. without a sample list).
--n-chunks N_CHUNKS
Request N_CHUNKS output chunks per sample for modern Analysis scripts, overriding the sample's n-chunks setting.
--stride STRIDE
Set the event stride for modern Analysis scripts, overriding the sample's stride setting.
--test-file TEST_FILE
Specify the test file for modern Analysis scripts. This option requires --test.
--bench
Output benchmark results to a JSON file.
-j NCPUS, --ncpus NCPUS (deprecated), --n-threads NTHREADS
Set number of jobs (threads) to use. The default number of threads to use is 1. To use all threads available on the machine specify -1.
-g, --graph
The computational graph of the analysis will be generated.
--graph-path GRAPH_PATH
Location where the computational graph of the analysis should be stored. Only paths with .dot and .png extensions are accepted.
ANALYSIS ARGUMENTS
Command line arguments which will not be parsed by the framework and will be passed directly to the analysis script.

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

FCCDICTSDIR
Controls search path for the process dictionaries. The default value is /cvmfs/fcc.cern.ch/FCCDicts/.
